questions.text: What maximum percentage of total account equity do most professional day traders recommend risking on any single trade?
questions.explanation: The narration states that most professional traders use 2 percent as a maximum risk limit per trade.

questions.text: True or false: A protective stop loss is an automated exit order placed with your broker to cut losses at a predefined price.
questions.explanation: A stop loss automatically exits a position at a set price level to limit downside risk.

questions.text: To maintain a mathematical edge over time, what is the minimum recommended risk-to-reward ratio for a trade setup?
questions.explanation: A minimum risk-to-reward ratio of one to two ensures potential gains double potential losses on every trade.

questions.text: True or false: If an account reaches its maximum overall drawdown limit, traders should double their position size to recover capital quickly.
questions.explanation: Reaching a maximum overall drawdown limit requires cutting position sizes in half to protect capital.
